conviction_note: The Q4 update (Aug-Oct) carries new LFL/occupancy KPIs but the FY26 EPS line was guided to the lower half of 39.6-42.4p on 3 Sep and reconfirmed on 15 Oct, so the guide is effectively pre-released. The only fresh counterparty, Big Yellow's 16 Nov interims (worse October occupancy, weak domestic demand), has already been followed by a 7.7% fall in SAFE (563.5p to 520p). Findings net to -0.3 on weaker KPIs. p_up sits at 51 because the drawdown appears to price that read-across, so the scaled number is about zero against an abs move of 3.5%. The two numbers differ in sign but both are close to zero.

findings.finding: Big Yellow's 16 Nov interims say UK self-storage occupancy deteriorated in October. BYG lost 65,000 sq ft (0.9% of MLA) since end-September against 25,000 a year earlier, its LFL occupancy gap widened from -0.3ppt to -1.1ppt, it cites 'continued weakness in domestic demand' and new supply in London, and it reports a 10% EPRA NAV fall on cap-rate expansion. This points to a softer Safestore UK Q4, whose October month overlaps.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 TU (3 Sep 2026) with LFL slowing to +1.9% and the EPS trim: -3.04%. Q4 TU 2025 with LFL +3.3%: +3.3%. Q1 2026 TU: -0.13%.
findings.original_quote: In the current year we have lost 65,000 sq ft (0.9% of maximum lettable area “MLA”) since the end of September, compared to a loss of 25,000 sq ft (0.4% of MLA) at the same stage last year, with continued weakness in domestic demand. The like-for-like gap in occupancy is now 1.1 ppts compared to 0.3 ppts at 30 September.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. SAFE fell from 563.5p (16 Nov close) to 520p (25 Nov), -7.7% against BYG's -4.4%, so the tape has reacted to the read-across. What remains is that Safestore's own UK and Paris figures have not been published. The finding is kept small because it is a peer proxy, Safestore's Q4 is two-thirds Aug-Sep, and the price has already moved.
findings.independence: Shurgard's Q3 2026 same-store revenue slowed to +1.8% CER (https://www.insideselfstorage.com/facility-operators/shurgard-self-storage-releases-third-quarter-2026-financial-results). Safestore's own Q3 LFL occupancy was already -0.8ppt (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/safestore-holdings--safe/third-quarter-trading-update/9752862)

findings.finding: FY2026 EPS is effectively pre-released. The company guided to the lower half of 39.6-42.4p on 3 Sep and on 15 Oct (two weeks before the 31 Oct year end) said performance was 'consistent with the guidance', so the Q4 update most likely reconfirms an EPS inside the guided range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS trimmed to the lower half on 3 Sep 2026: -3.04%. 'In line with consensus' Q4 TU on 27 Nov 2025: +3.3%.
findings.original_quote: There will be no new disclosures on current trading with the Group’s overall performance consistent with the guidance provided in the Q3 trading update on 3 September 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The guide is public and repeated, so it is sized near zero. The small positive reflects the chance of relief on a reconfirmation after the 7.7% post-Big-Yellow drawdown, which a stock pricing an EPS miss would show. A miss below 39.6p is the tail, and the 15 Oct reconfirmation makes it unlikely.
findings.independence: Q3 TU footnote 9 gives the range 39.6-42.4p (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/safestore-holdings--safe/third-quarter-trading-update/9752862)

findings.finding: In the Q3 TU Safestore said it is 'reviewing the phasing of the 2027-28 UK pipeline'. If the Q4 update concludes the review with deferred UK capex, it is a capital-allocation item that lowers funding needs while gilts and valuations are under pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The review was announced in the -3.04% Q3 TU alongside the EPS trim.
findings.original_quote: Given current trading conditions, we are reviewing the phasing of the 2027-28 UK pipeline in line with our disciplined capital allocation; the pipeline itself is unchanged
findings.why_not_priced: The outcome and timing of the review are not public; nothing from the 15 Oct strategy event reached the wire I could find. It is an inference that the TU carries it rather than the January finals, so the finding is kept small.

findings.why_not_priced: It is a public RNS but a small purchase by a non-executive. It is weak evidence that the board did not see a Q4 below guidance, and it is sized accordingly.

findings.finding: Paris LFL is likely negative again in Q4. Q3 Paris LFL revenue was -2.5% with LFL occupancy -6.2ppt as new company stores cannibalise, and the Q4 2025 comp is +2.0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Paris weakness was part of the -3.04% Q3 TU reaction.
findings.original_quote: Like-for-like Paris revenue for the quarter down 2.5%, reflecting the expected transfer of enquiries from new customers to our non-LFL stores together with reduced occupancy in large units
findings.why_not_priced: The company called the trend 'expected' and it is already in the FY guide, so it is mostly priced. It is filed only for the tougher comp. Total French revenue still grows on non-LFL stores, so net of the rest of the company the effect is small.
findings.independence: Last year's Q4 TU Paris LFL comp of +2.0% (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/safestore-holdings--safe/fourth-quarter-trading-update/9259970)

findings.finding: The Continental peer Shurgard slowed to +1.8% CER same-store revenue in Q3 2026, consistent with a subdued European self-storage backdrop for Safestore's Paris and Expansion markets.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy published two weeks ago and likely priced. It is filed small because Safestore's Expansion markets were growing LFL at +11.6% in Q3, against the trend.
findings.independence: Big Yellow's interims (finding 1), a different market

The lean (+0.86, squeeze component) and the 7.7% drawdown since Big Yellow's interims argue the negative read-across is already priced, so p_up is held at 51 rather than below 50.
